The proposed design incorporates the left and right hand identification and the height determination to address accuracy issues from variations in user's height or body size. By integrating the estimation data for angles, user's height, and handedness, the horizontal and vertical SVM classifiers will be pre-trained. After the SVM classifiers are well trained, the combination results from both SVM classifiers enables the prediction of the user's area of interests. Experimental results with four, six, and eight grid divisions on the display reveals that the average identifying accuracies for horizontal and vertical grid classification can be up to 94% and 83%, respectively. By height adjusted information, the horizontal and vertical classification accuracies of the SVM classifiers can improve by 11% and 20% respectively within corresponding height ranges. For the embedded device implementation, the YOLO model and SVM classifier are deployed on the Jetson AGX Orin platform to achieve an average processing speed of 15 frames per second.

articleTitle: DRL-Based Energy-Efficient Pilot and Data Power Control for Uplink Cell-Free Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper studies an energy-efficient joint pilot-and data-power control for uplink cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-mMIMO) networks. We first formulate an uplink energy efficiency (EE) maximization problem under the minimum required uplink data rate constraint. The formulated problem is non-convex and therefore hard to solve using conventional optimization algorithms. To solve the problem, we propose a deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based scheme. Specifically, we use proximal policy optimization (PPO) algorithm. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed PPO-based scheme can significantly enhance the EE of the uplink CF-mMIMO networks.

articleTitle: Revisiting 3D Multi-Modal Medical Image Generation: Model Configurations for Brain MR Image Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Multi-modal magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) has become a widely used tool for segmenting subregions of brain glioblastomas. However, acquiring a complete set of multi-modal MRI images is constrained by time, cost, and patient movement during prolonged MRI scans. In this paper, we address this issue by exploring various model configurations to develop an optimal algorithm for synthesizing missing modalities. We validated our model using the Brain MR Image Synthesis Benchmark (BraSyn) dataset. Our results show that the proposed method generates high-quality synthetic images that closely match the ground truth of the missing modalities while maintaining the performance of downstream tumor segmentation in this scenario.

articleTitle: Development of a Real-Time Wireless Multi-Node Metal Pipeline Localization System via Bluetooth Link
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Several efforts have been approached to minimize the limitations and risks associated with current methods of locating underground pipelines in construction projects, especially during excavation operations. Traditional methods rely on flags to mark the general location of pipelines, which can be imprecise and lead to accidents. Excavation damage is a significant cause of pipeline failures, resulting in injuries, fatalities, and financial losses. To address these issues, we have been studied to accurately locate the underground ferromagnetic pipeline using magnetic anomaly detection approach using multi-dimensional magnetic sensor array using a smart external magnetic interference cancellation algorithm under the lab-based setting. To expand the successful approach in the actual construction setting, we proposed the development of a smart, real-time, wireless multi-node sensor system that uses magnetic anomaly detection algorithm on a custom smartphone app. This system aims to improve the accuracy of pipeline location detection during excavation, thereby reducing the potential for accidents and enhancing safety on construction sites. We have successfully designed and assembled the multi-node metal pipeline localization system via BLE. By attaching three modules on the excavator bucket, we were able to collect the sensor data using a custom-designed app and estimate the distance from the pipe.

articleTitle: Robust Object Detection Across Diverse Environments Using Contrastive Learning-Based Domain Adaptation*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The performance of object detection in road-driving scenarios is critically important but often hindered by challenges such as occlusion, time-of-day changes (e.g., day and night), and adverse weather conditions (e.g., rain, snow, fog), which lead to significant performance degradation. To overcome these challenges, this paper introduces a contrastive learning-based approach that integrates three specialized loss functions: Predicted Object Loss (POL), Missed Object Loss (MOL), and Distribution Alignment Loss (DAL) within a domain adaptation framework. The proposed method generates noise datasets from clean images, pairs these clean and noise images, and utilizes them as input for the model, with a focus on rain and night-time conditions during training. POL aligns the feature distributions of predicted objects between clean and noise images, while MOL adjusts the features of objects missed in the noise images to align with those in the clean images. Additionally, the model is trained to enhance object-background separation by increasing the distance between object features and background features in noise images. DAL further reduces the domain gap by minimizing the feature distribution discrepancies between noise and clean datasets. This approach not only reduces domain discrepancies but also improves detection accuracy, robustness in noisy environments, and generalization across diverse conditions. Experiments conducted on the KITTI dataset demonstrate the effectiveness of this method, with notable improvements in mAP performance across various noise conditions, including rain, night-time, fog, and snow, derived from clean images.

articleTitle: Reference Image Estimation for Enhanced Video Display Field Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Video Display Field Communication (DFC) is a frequency-based Display-to-Camera (D2C) communication technology where the display and camera act as transmitter and receiver, respectively. Data is transmitted over the D2C link in the form of an image or video, carefully embedded to minimize any distortion to the user's viewing experience. Video-DFC enables the transmission of large amounts of data by embedding it within each video frame, based on a frame packet structure. In this paper, we present experimental results and analysis focused on the structure and performance improvements of Video-DFC. Previous Video-DFC proposed a method of inserting a color code-based 4-point block pattern at the four corners of the final transmitted image frame. Further research demonstrated the potential for improving the performance of the Video-DFC system by using interpolation to estimate the reference image needed for data extraction. Additionally, the system's performance was validated in real-world conditions by evaluating the Achievable Data Rate (ADR) according to the frame packet structure. Notably, a data transmission rate improvement of approximately 2.3 kbps was observed with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{N}{=}$</tex> 10, confirming enhanced performance compared to the conventional single reference image-based Video-DFC.

articleTitle: Helmet Detection of Motobike Riders in Real-World Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Automated video surveillance systems for detecting helmet-wearing by motorbike riders and passengers play a critical role in enhancing road safety and increasing the efficiency of law enforcement. However, accurately detecting small objects, such as helmets, remains a technical challenge under varying environmental conditions. In this paper, we propose an ensemble strategy that combines a CNN-based model (YOLOvl0) with a transformer-based model (DE-DETRs) to detect violations of motorcycle helmet-wearing regulations. The DE-DETRs model utilizes multi-scale features to detect small objects, while YOLOvl0 offers real-time performance without the need for Non-Maximum Suppression (NMS). To combine the predictions from these two models, we apply the Weighted Box Fusion (WBF) technique, enabling more precise object detection. Additionally, to address the issue of data imbalance, we employ Curriculum of Data Augmentation (CUDA)-based data augmentation techniques to optimize the model's training performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed ensemble model outperforms individual models, and WBF -based post-processing effectively improves detection accuracy across various scenarios.

articleTitle: An Improved User Interface Checking Function Considering Multiple Platforms for Flutter Programming Learning Assistant System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: To support learning Dart programming on the Flutter cross-platform development framework, we have developed the Flutter Programming Learning Assistant System (FPLAS). FPLAS incorporates a Docker-based Flutter environment with Visual Studio Code and five foundational exercise projects. The user interface checking function was implemented to automatically assess students' source codes by executing them and comparing the resulting UI images on the web platform with the correct reference images. However, we only considered the web platform on Windows in the user interface checking function, although the same Dart code may generate different UI images depending on the target platform and operating system. It is essential to account for these variations in the function. In this paper, we improve the UI checking function to absorb the differences in the output UI image across multiple platforms including iOS, Android, and web, by preparing correct images for each platform. For evaluations, we applied the proposal to the UI image files generated in the five exercises and confirmed the validity and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Infrared Thermal Imaging for Embedded Child Presence Detection System: Feasibility and Performance Evaluation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In the automotive industry, regulations and standards mandate that Child Presence Detection (CPD) systems must be installed. Most current CPD systems utilize radar or visible cameras to identify the presence or absence of objects based on bio-signals or movement information. However, these systems cannot determine if an emergency situation, such as heatstroke, occurs as the temperature inside the vehicle rises. In this paper, we propose an architecture for a thermal imaging-based CPD system that can perform simultaneous object detection, recognition, and status assessment, while also monitoring the internal environment of the vehicle. We further evaluate the feasibility of this thermal imaging-based CPD system in meeting the performance requirements outlined by regulations and standards for in-cabin use.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer System with Optimal Dead-Time Tracking Class-D Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a cross-connected (CC) wireless power transceiver (WPT) with an optimal dead-time controller (ODTC). The ODTC is designed to achieve zero-voltage-switching (ZVS) in a class-D power amplifier, reducing switching losses. This reduction in switching losses directly contributes to improved overall system efficiency. Furthermore, the proposed controller can quickly and accurately adjust the dead-time, responding effectively to any variations or changes in the system. This adjustment capability not only ensures high efficiency but also safe operation. The simulation results demonstrate the ODTC's ability to control the dead-time effectively.

articleTitle: Fusion of 3D-2D Data for Drivable Area Detection and Road Condition Analysis in Assistive Quadruped Robots for the Visually Impaired
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a system designed for a quadruped robot that assists visually impaired individuals by analyzing road conditions and detecting drivable areas. The system integrates 3D point cloud data from Lidar with 2D semantic segmentation from RGB cameras, enabling a comprehensive understanding of the environment through a 3D-2D data fusion approach. By evaluating critical road properties such as flatness, material uniformity, slope, and vertical clearance, the system ensures safe and efficient navigation in complex terrains. To enhance depth perception, we incorporate depth completion techniques, allowing for real-time road condition assessment. The fusion of Lidar and RGB data creates accurate drivable area maps, enabling the robot to make informed decisions about path planning and obstacle avoidance. The proposed system is validated through real-world experiments, demonstrating its effectiveness in assisting visually impaired users by providing reliable navigation across diverse environments. The contributions of this work include the development of a robust road condition analysis module and the fusion of 3D-2D data for enhanced semantic segmentation, advancing the capabilities of assistive robotic systems for visually impaired navigation.

articleTitle: Korean News Summarization with Contrasts by Augmenting Counterfactual Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: We introduce a method utilizing counterfactual data to increase performance for an abstractive summarization with contrasts. Previous summarization studies concentrate on summary generation given only input text; however, our method incorporates counterfactual data that includes hypothetical scenarios different from the original text. By augmenting the model with these counterfactual examples, it learns to identify key information and its contrasts more effectively, leading to more refined and accurate summaries. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed method outperforms traditional methods and general LLM prompting methods, showcasing its potential in generating contrastive summaries.

articleTitle: Collaborative Intelligence Framework with Skip-Decoder for Balanced Edge Power and Cloud Cost in Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This study proposes a cost-effective distributed inference framework for real-time object detection in edge environments. Due to the resource constraints of edge devices, Col-laborative Intelligence (CI) has become increasingly important in enabling efficient distributed inference between cloud and edge. This study leverages the YOLOv7 model to analyze inference latency between edge devices and the server, and presents strategies to address issues related to the power consumption of edge devices and the costs associated with cloud usage. Additionally, a feature map recovery technique called Skip-decoder is introduced to reduce network latency. This novel CI model architecture aims to optimize the use of edge resources, thereby reducing cloud expenses and enhancing real-time object detection performance.

articleTitle: Bed Rise Prediction IoT System under Varying Blanket Conditions using Multimodal Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In this paper, we propose bed rise prediction IoT system under varying blanket conditions using an accelerometer and a low-resolution infrared sensor as multimodal machine learning. The system predicts bed rise actions based on CNN-LSTM from the movements observed prior to a bed rise action, therefore we aim to reduce some risks, i.e., elderly individuals injuring themselves and falls. Furthermore, we investigate how combining two sensor data affects the results under three conditions: no blanket, thin blanket, and thick blanket. The result has demonstrated the accuracy improved slightly under the blanket conditions when using both, compared to using only infrared data. Additionally, we have indicated that the variability in prediction results based on the initial weight values can be reduced by only adjusting the learning rate.

articleTitle: Performance Characterization of CXL Memory Expander: Impact on Read and Write Latencies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: As data processing requirements and memory de-mands driven by Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, and In-Memory Database technologies continue to grow exponen-tially, the need for systems with greater memory capacity is increasing. This trend highlights the limitations of traditional Dual In-Line Memory Module (DIMM) interfaces due to CPU package constraints in server systems. Compute Express Link (CXL) technology, leveraging the PCIe interface, has emerged as a promising solution to expand memory capacity and bandwidth. This paper evaluates the performance of ASIC-based CXL memory expanders on Intel's latest server systems. Our experimental results demonstrate that while CXL memory expanders offer significant memory capacity benefits, they also introduce additional latency. Notably, read operations are more sensitive to latency changes compared to write operations, resulting in a more pronounced latency increase for reads. This study highlights the tradeoffs associated with CXL memory expanders and provides insights into optimizing memory configurations for diverse workloads, emphasizing the importance of considering latency impacts on different types of operations.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Transfer Learning Using RNN and LSTM for Room Temperature Prediction Considering Occupancy Variation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Enhancing room temperature prediction performance is beneficial for optimizing air conditioning control and supporting other applications. While previous studies have explored the effective use of prediction models across different buildings through transfer learning, performance under varying occupancy remains unclear. In this study, we evaluated the effectiveness of transfer learning by applying a model trained on data from an office with constant occupancy in Nagoya to a variable occupancy scenario in Hokkaido, adding randomness. The results showed that transfer learning significantly improved prediction accuracy with varying occupancy. The greatest improvements were in short-term predictions up to 1 minute ahead, with a 72% error reduction, and in long-term predictions up to 24 hours ahead, with a 47% reduction. In the future, We plan to further enhance accuracy by refining model and adjusting data used.

articleTitle: An Obstacle Avoidance System for Visual Impaired People Based on Object Tracking Algorithm and Semantic Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Many visually impaired people face safety issues when walking outside. Providing a safe method to guide such individuals in complex road situations is a widely discussed challenge. With the advancement of deep learning, we have proposed an obstacle avoidance system to address this problem. In this system, a 360-degree camera is used as an input device to record the surrounding environment of users. Deep learning technologies, specifically ByteTrack and MMSegmentation, are employed to process the video data. As a result, the system provides multi-modal feedback to users, helping them avoid obstacles.

articleTitle: A Study on Digital Twin Modules that Support Digital Twinning of the Physical World
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: A digital twin is a physical entity that is replicated as logical information and expressed in the digital world. The logical information in the digital world includes information such as the entity's properties, characteristics, behaviors and events, and is synchronized with the physical entity in real time. However, the lack of a common definition and understanding of digital twins, the difficulty of integrating distributed and isolated backend data, and the lack of a standardized information model to increase interoperability between data sources are hindering the adoption of digital twins. In this paper, we aim to implement and study a digital twin module that can model entities as logical information and support synchronization between physical and digital entities to make it easier to build digital twins.

articleTitle: Initial Attempt at Automated Vulnerability Fixing of Obfuscated Smart Contracts Using a Large Language Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Countermeasures against vulnerabilities are essential for the security of smart contracts. Some recent studies have focused on automated vulnerability repair using large language models (LLMs). However, the ability of LLMs to fix unknown contracts is still unclear. To address this problem, we applied Code Llama LLM to a real-world smart contract with a vulnerability and its obfuscated version, assuming that the obfuscated version could be considered an unknown contract. We obtained three fixes generated by the LLM for each contract. Of these three, one fix was successful for each contract. While some fixes removed the vulnerability, they also altered the functionality of the contract. No clear difference was observed between the original and obfuscated contracts in terms of the LLM's repairing capability.

articleTitle: Weakly Supervised Video Anomaly Detection Using Dynamic-Weighted Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Recent studies have shown that using video and text together works well in weakly supervised video anomaly detection (WSVAD) tasks. However, existing methods often struggle with the presence of both normal and abnormal frames within abnormal videos, leading to suboptimal training and inaccurate anomaly predictions. Additionally, the misalignment of video and textual representations can result in the loss of important contextual information, further hindering performance. To address these issues, we propose a novel approach for weakly supervised video anomaly detection (WSVAD) using dynamic-weighted feature fusion (DWFF). Leveraging vision-language models (VLMs) such as contrastive language-image pre-training (CLIP), we enhance anomaly detection by aligning video and textual representations. Our approach introduces dynamic weighting that emphasizes abnormal frames during training and employs a fusion of video-level and frame-level features to improve anomaly prediction accuracy. We combine frame-level similarities with class embeddings and video-level features, enhancing the model's ability to capture temporal dependencies and refine anomaly detection. We evaluate our method on two benchmark datasets, the UCF-Crime and the XD-Violence, demonstrating its superiority over existing state-of-the-art methods. Our results show significant improvements in detection accuracy, highlighting the effectiveness of dynamic weighting and feature fusion techniques in WSVAD tasks.

articleTitle: LiDAR on a Budget: Driving Global Safety Innovations Across Developing Countries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The adoption of LiDAR (Light Detection and Ranging) technology in vehicular safety systems, notably Collision Avoidance Systems (CAS), has predominantly been a feature of vehicles in developed countries, facilitated by the technology's advanced capabilities and effectiveness. However, the high cost of LiDAR sensors has significantly limited their integration into vehicles in developing countries. This paper addresses this challenge by exploring the development and implementation of a cost-effective LiDAR-based CAS. By demonstrating the feasibility of using budget-conscious LiDAR sensors, this study aims to achieve substantial improvements in traffic safety without incurring the premium costs typically associated with these systems. The detailed processes of system design, sensor integration and empirical validation highlighted in this research underscore the potential for advanced safety systems to become more accessible and economically viable across a broader geographic spectrum.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation in UAV-IRS Communication System with IRS Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In this study, we evaluated the performance of the achievable rate in an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) communication system, considering the IRS radiation pattern. First, we modeled the IRS channel taking the radiation pattern into account in a scenario where a UAV supports a user using a fixed IRS. Then, we configured the IRS phase shift matrix to maximize the channel gain. Through experiments, we compared scenarios with and without consid-ering the IRS radiation pattern, emphasizing the importance of developing communication techniques that consider the IRS radiation pattern.

articleTitle: In Vivo Ultrahigh-Resolution Quantitative OCT Imaging in Lungs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Pulmonary diseases such as asthma and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) are significant global health challenges, characterized by extensive remodeling of small airways. Conventional imaging modalities like spirometry and computed tomography are limited in their ability to visualize these microstructural changes, hindering effective evaluation of disease progression and treatment outcomes. In this study, we developed and utilized an 800-nm ultrahigh-resolution diffractive optical coherence tomography (OCT) system for in vivo imaging of small airway microstructures. The system achieves a lateral resolution of approximately 7.2 μm and an axial resolution of 1.7 μm in tissue, allowing detailed visualization of critical airway components, including smooth muscle, epithelium, basement membrane, and cartilage. We employed a 1.8-mm-outer diameter imaging catheter to access and image small airways. Validation through comparative histological analysis confirmed the accuracy of our OCT system. Furthermore, we utilized deep learning algorithms to achieve automated segmentation of airway microstructures. Our results demonstrate the potential of this advanced imaging tool in providing new insights into airway remodeling in diseases such as asthma and COPD, as well as in assessing the efficacy of therapeutic interventions.

articleTitle: QRS Complex Detection Using Tahar Differentiator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: A signal from an electrocardiogram, often known as an ECG, is one of the physiological signals that can be used to assess a person's health and identify any diseases that may be present. Extraction of the QRS component from the electrocardiogram signal has been a significant area of research for a number of years. For the purpose of QRS detection, the Pan-Tompkins method is a well-known and commonly utilised technique. This method includes a digital differentiator as one of its basic parts. Over the course of this research, an attempt is made to investigate the operation of the Pan Tompkins algorithm by substituting the digital differentiator block with the infinite impulse response digital differentiators. All of the simulations are executed with the help of MATLAB, and the outcomes that are obtained are comparable to those acquired using the traditional method.

articleTitle: Experimental Fire Detection and Alarm System Based on the Integration of IoT and Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Fires are considered a risk that causes human death and property loss. To reduce fire damage, fires must be detected and warned promptly. This paper aims to design and experimentally implement a fully-function fire detection and warning system. The developed system is based on a Wireless Sensor Network (WSN) that includes various nodes distributed across the city. Each node has two main blocks which are the image processing and communication blocks. The image processing block applies the EfficientN et B0 model to detect the fire and smoke, whereas the communication block uses the Module 4G to contact the house owner over a mobile phone network and LoRa gateway to send the signal warning to the fire center over the a LoRaWAN. The Module 4G is responsible for sending captured images of suspected fire if any to the house owner's device for getting his/her acknowledgement. Then an urgent alarm message consisting of fire position and risk level are sent to the fire center if the fire is acknowledged by the house owner, otherwise, the alarm is ceased. Besides, the proposed system is installed the gas sensor, smoke sensor, water spray system and light-sound alarm to augment the reliability of fire detection. The proposed system is experimentally demonstratedand achieved positive results: Delay time sending from the proposed fire detection system to the user is recorded as 5 seconds and from the user to the fire center is recorded as 10 seconds, within a LoRaWAN coverage of1.5km.

articleTitle: Human Trajectory Prediction Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Navigating safely within buildings is crucial for mobile robots, especially in environments shared with humans. To address this, we propose a novel method that leverages LiDAR sensor data to identify and predict human movement patterns. Our approach integrates spatial data analysis with a Kalman filter to enhance prediction accuracy. Comprehensive experimental results demonstrate the method's effectiveness, indicating its potential to improve mobile robot navigation in indoor environments. This innovation paves the way for more harmonious and efficient human-robot interaction in shared indoor spaces.

articleTitle: EA-FCM: An Energy-Efficient 3D Path Planning Algorithm for Multiple UAVs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: A multi-Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) system improves operational efficiency in applications, such as reconnaissance, disaster relief, agriculture, and logistics. Maintaining balanced energy consumption among UAVs is crucial for mission success, as energy imbalance can cause premature battery depletion and mission failure. This study proposes an optimization approach that enables balanced energy distribution during missions where multiple UAVs simultaneously cover an area, while also decoupling energy consumption into specific flight modes to allow for more precise energy calculations. Unlike previous research focused mainly on distance-based path optimization, this study prioritizes maintaining energy balance across UAVs. The proposed model is compared with an optimized Fuzzy C-Means clustering algorithm in terms of the energy consumption distribution among UAVs. Simulation results confirm the proposed model reduces both the variance and the coefficient of variation in energy consumption, enhancing mission efficiency across scenarios.

articleTitle: Towards Eight-Bit Quantization for 3D U-Net Medical Image Segmentation via ROI-Based Calibration and Background-Aware Shift
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: 3D U-Net medical image segmentation is essential for precise diagnosis and treatment planning but comes with massive bandwidth requirements and considerable computational costs. Eight-bit fixed-point quantization is crucial for efficient 3D U-Net inference on modern deep learning accelerators. However, quantizing a 3D U-Net model is non-trivial and frequently leads to unfavorable accuracy degradation. We empirically observed that large range imbalances between tumor/non-tumor voxels and foreground/background areas are the main contributing factors. Based on these findings, we propose an eight-bit quantization method with a simple yet effective ROI-based calibration and a background shift that captures outliers in tumor areas to avoid accuracy degradation. Moreover, our method incorporates instance normalization folding, which eliminates computation-intensive operations during inference. Experimental results on the KITS19 dataset show that the proposed method with integer-only arithmetic achieves a negligible accuracy drop, i.e., 0.4%p in the dice score, compared to the FP32 model.

articleTitle: Curtailing Harvest Waste with IoT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The increase in human population and satisfaction needs has precedented impacts on natural resources inflicting the cost of living. Food is a vital source for living, tracing back to its source reveals the underlying concern of harvest waste. Therefore, effective management of crops supply chain is critical. Amid it, Internet of Things technology is gaining popularity in tackling concerns and eliminating tedious tasks. This paper investigates the utilization of IoT devices and data analytics to track and enhance different phases of the harvest chain. The proposed framework, Harvesters IoT System, breaks down interconnected monitoring systems into subsystems to improve interoperability and provide simplicity for management facilitation. By leveraging real-time data, predictive analytics, and automated processes, this framework addresses inefficiencies in the supply chain, ensuring that crops are harvested, stored, and distributed with minimal wastage.

articleTitle: Commercial-Off-the-Shelf (COTS) Wearable Elbow Joint Angle Measurement System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Measuring joint angles is crucial for kinematic analysis of human movement. The measurement of range of motion (ROM) is particularly essential for evaluation of a patient's joint function in physical therapy and rehabilitation. Physical therapists and physicians typically use a mechanical goniometer to measure joint angles in clinical settings. However, this measurement is often limited by low accuracy, limited resolution, and observation error. This study presents a commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) wearable elbow joint angle measurement system, which would enhance the measurement accuracy. The accuracy of the system was evaluated in two test setups: 1) desktop test setup without human subjects and 2) wearable test setup with human subjects. In the test without human subjects, the angle measurement was repeated for five times at the angles varied from 60° to 180° by 10° increments. In the test with human subjects, nine healthy human subjects participated in the experiment. Three representative elbow joint angles between 60° and 180° were measured for 10 times at each subject (60°, 120°, and 180°). The average error of the measured angle was 0.52±0.34 % (AVR±STE) at the desktop test without human subjects. The average error of the measured angle at the test with nine human subjects was -0.29±0.10%. These results indicate that the presented system can measure the elbow joint angle in high accuracy and consistency.

articleTitle: Improving Position-Based Alignment for AUV's Localization Through Optimal Data Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper describes a method for improving the performance of the position-based in-motion alignment algorithm used to accurately estimate the initial heading of AUVs(Autonomous Underwater Vehicles). The alignment algorithm in prior research used GPS(Global Positioning System) positions and navigation-estimated positions to correct the heading angle. However, significant errors in some GPS data adversely affected the accuracy of heading bias estimation. To resolve this issue, this study divides the position data into candidate data and validation data. The optimal sample for estimating heading bias is then identified from the candidate data using the validation data. The proposed algorithm is verified through experiments using sensor datasets acquired from real sea experiments.

articleTitle: Action Recognition Based on Lightweight SlowFast Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In this paper, we propose action recognition based on lightweight SlowFast networks. We propose a lightweight neural network architecture combined with a fast and slow network to perform temporal feature extraction and spatial feature extraction through two different channels. After fusion, the accuracy of action recognition can be increased. The experimental results show that the proposed method can achieve high-precision action recognition and reduce the computational complexity of the neural network.

articleTitle: Thermal Design of GaN Power Devices in Wafer Level Chip Scale Package (WLCSP) for Automotive EPS Motor Drivers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Since wafer-level chip-scale packages (WLCSPs) offer advantages of reducing parasitic inductance and package size, as well as enhancing thermal conductivity, this work comprises gallium nitride (GaN) devices in a WLCSP for automotive electric power steering (EPS) motor drivers. We present a thermal design of WLCSP GaN power transistor devices. The effectiveness and usefulness of our design are verified through thermal performance experiments and an in-vehicle EPS evaluation of steering assistance performance.

articleTitle: FT-IR Analysis Results of Flexible Substrates According to Various Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This study focuses on characterizing flexible substrate materials, especially polyimide (PI) films. We investigated the complexity of molecular structure analysis applied to the film through heat treatment of the substrate before and after rolling to analyze the mechanical properties of the flexible substrate in actual operation. Our experiments were conducted by intentionally adjusting the number of rolling cycles and temperature parameters applied to the flexible substrate. Afterwards, a comprehensive sample analysis was performed using Fourier transform infrared (FT-IR) spectroscopy, which allowed us to thoroughly investigate the molecular composition and structural integrity of the substrate. We also observed changes in the molecular structure due to physical stress through scratch tests on the heat-treated film after the rolling process. Our experimental results confirmed that molecules with weak bonds tend to dissociate under physical stresses such as rolling.

articleTitle: Fully Approximate Computing for Efficient Multi-Bit DNN Inference in CIM Arrays
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Compute-in-memory (CIM) architectures are becoming increasingly important for real-time, low-power deep neural network (DNN) inference due to their ability to perform matrix-vector multiplications directly within memory. However, conventional CIM systems often struggle to balance efficient data processing with the computational demands of large-scale DNNs, particularly in scenarios involving sparse data. These systems tend to perform unnecessary computations, leading to reduced throughput and increased energy consumption. In this paper, we propose a novel CIM architecture that eliminates certain multi-bit operations, thereby avoiding unnecessary calculations and optimizing resource usage. By leveraging a new numerical system specifically tailored for CIM array operations, we reduce computing cycles by 50% compared to traditional methods, with only a minimal accuracy loss of 1%.

articleTitle: On Collective Reboot to Mitigate Botnet Threats in Low-Observability IoT Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In order to exterminate botnets that have infected IoT devices, we proposed a method of rebooting on a per-area basis rather than on a per-device basis. We were able to confirm that this method can efficiently disinfect a botnet by rebooting an entire area that has been significantly infected by a self-propagating and repeatedly occurring botnet and boldly recovering the area. However, not all botnets are observable. Therefore, we propose an effective countermeasure in IoT networks with low observability. In IoT networks with low observability, some Bots frequently evade disinfection by frequently moving back and forth between the boundaries of the regions where they are collectively rebooted. Therefore, by defining the boundary of the region as a special region, we can prevent bots from frequently coming and going on the boundary and improve the disinfection efficiency. Simulation results confirmed that this method can suppress the number of botnets to about 20% or less of the total number of botnets in most steps.

articleTitle: Ensemble Learning Algorithm-Based Air Leakage Detection Technology in Pneumatic Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The issue of air leakage in machines has occurred for a long time due to imbalances in compressed air supply and instability of pneumatic machines. As a solution to this problem, real-time monitoring and control methods have been proposed to address the air leakage issue. However, such solutions result in monetary loss due to the need to stop equipment operation. In addition, conventional solutions focus on post-processing, which has the limitation of not being able to maintain the operational efficiency of the system. To solve the air leakage issue without decreasing machine efficiency, this paper proposes a method to detect air leakage several minutes in advance using various IoT sensor data collected from the machine. Using the proposed method, it is confirmed that it is possible to detect air leakage several minutes in advance with at least 90% accuracy.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Approach to Detect Air Leakage in the System Using IoT Sensor Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Compressed air is widely used as a reliable means of transporting energy in a variety of industries. However, air leaks in compressed air systems cause significant inefficiencies, resulting in significant financial losses and harm to the environment. A common solution is for a specialist to explore the site with equipment to find out if and where the leak is located. However, this solution has the limitation of requiring pneumatic equipment to be shut down at the time of the meter reading, resulting in reduced productivity and increased costs. For these reason, a lot of research is being done to monitor compressed air pressure using sensors to find leaks. In this paper, we propose a machine learning-based approach that combines DTW-based K-means clustering with the XGBoost model. The proposed method is validated by simulation using data collected from the demonstration site, and achieved an accuracy of 78.3%, AUC of 0.884, and F1 score of 0.775.

articleTitle: Hyperbolic-Based Tree Edit Distance as Similarity of User Behavior
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In this paper, we evaluate the similarity between users' behavior by applying tree edit distance (TED) to tree representations generated through hyperbolic metric learning methods. Understanding user behavior similarity is an essential task in e-commerce, as it can be modeled as a tree-like structure where each action corresponds to a node, representing the user's possible next move. Analyzing user behavior similarity through the lens of advertising costs provides insight into the effort needed to shift from one user's action pattern to another. We explore the benefits of using tree edit distance for user behavior analysis and further consider their similarity under hyperbolic metric embedding methods.

articleTitle: A Handheld Electronic Stethoscope for Non-Invasive Cuffless Blood Pressure Detection Using Real-Time PCG and PPG Signal Recording
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Regular blood pressure monitoring at home has been proven to mitigate substantial risks associated with heart disease. However, existing gold-standard blood pressure devices are required to be more active and user-friendly for monitoring over a long period. This study introduces a handheld electronic stethoscope with a non-invasive method for calculating blood pressure based on vascular transit time. The wearable device is designed to be user-friendly while offering useful visual and numeric information. The stethoscope demonstrates a promising functional performance with a signal-to-noise ratio exceeding 32 dB across all cases, implying highly reliable PCG recording. Initial blood pressure measuring conducted with seven volunteers yielded mean absolute errors of 6.6 mmHg and 5.13 mmHg for diastolic and systolic blood pressure, respectively.

articleTitle: Design of an Approximate Multiplier with Error Recovery and Hardware Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel design for an approximate multiplier using an approximate 4-2 compressor, expanding upon conventional approaches. To address errors, it integrates a new error recovery module tailored for minimizing inaccuracies in approximate computations. The error recovery circuit is applied to the approximate compressor, which generates the maximum error. Furthermore, the design employs a truncation technique to simplify hardware complexity. By selectively truncating the lower 4-bits, it achieves a smaller footprint compared to previous models, resulting in reduced hardware complexity and lower power consumption. In essence, the proposed design presents an attractive balance between error recovery, hardware efficiency, delay, and power consumption.

articleTitle: Resonant Upconverter for Energy Harvesting in Low-Frequency and Low-Voltage Regimes
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In this paper, we have designed a suitable circuit for a harvester, specifically a carbon nanotube-based twistron, characterized by low frequency and low voltage. The entire system consists of a resonant upconversion part using a transformer and a voltage doubler part utilizing an active diode. This system is targeted for a twistron weighing 870 μg and operates when the input voltage exceeds 13 mV. When the input signal amplitude 15 mV and the frequency is 1 Hz, the final rectified voltage is 550 mV, with maximum output power of 1.18 μW. To achieve impedance matching between the harvester and the circuit, the weight of the harvester increases, resulting in a maximum output power of 17 μW, whose power conversion efficiency is 53 % and a rectified voltage of up to 990 mV in the circuit.

articleTitle: Design of High-Reliability LDO Regulator Incorporated with Additional Parasitic Bipolar Junction Transistor for Low Voltage Applicaiton
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: To ensure stable operation and reliability of the LDO regulator, a protection circuit against ESD surges is necessary. This paper focuses on effectively operating the LDO regulator in response to varying load currents while enhancing circuit reliability by integrating an ESD protection circuit at the IC level. The proposed LDO regulator achieves high reliability due to the inclusion of the ESD protection circuit. This is achieved by incorporating an LVTSCR-based ESD protection circuit in both the I/O and power clamps. Measurement results of the proposed circuit demonstrate that the LDO regulator can control the output voltage in response to changes in load current while maintaining voltage stability during ESD events. The LDO regulator, combined with the ESD protection circuit, was implemented using a 0.18 μm BCD process and maintained an undershoot of 13 mV and an overshoot of 49 mV at a load current of 100 mA.

articleTitle: Review-Based Unify MF and GraphSAGE to Enhancing the Recommendations Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In the age of information overload, effective rec-ommendation systems (RS) are crucial for helping users find relevant content. This study investigates the integration of traditional matrix factorization (MF) techniques with GraphSAGE to improve link prediction in recommendation systems (RS). The proposed approach overcomes the limitations of rating-based recommendation methods by applying sentiment analysis to review data to generate initial embeddings. Experiments on the Amazon movie and music datasets reveal that this hybrid model significantly improves prediction accuracy, evidenced by much higher AUC values. The findings demonstrate that combining MF and graph-based techniques leverages their strengths, offering a robust and reliable framework for predicting user preferences.

articleTitle: Optimizing UAV Swarm-Based Cooperative Transmission Using OTFS Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) are capable of enhancing communication coverage and facilitating critical communication networks through their mobility. Furthermore, the UAV swarms are being deployed across diverse civil and mil-itary applications. This paper is an extension of a work that utilizes orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) modulation in a UAV swarm-based cooperative transmission setup. Specifically, it focuses on the effect of the digital modulation type and the subcarrier spacing on the performance of the above-mentioned scenario. Through simulation, we offer valuable insights into designing effective communication setups, which improve the dependability and performance of UAV swarm communication systems.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Hybrid Satellite-Terrestrial Relaying Broadcast Networks Using Fountain Codes and NOMA
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In this article, we propose a hybrid satellite-terrestrial relaying (HSTR) network that combines Fountain codes (FCs) and non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA). In the proposed scheme, a satellite employs the NOMA technique to simultaneously transmit two Fountain packets to two clusters of terrestrial users, with the assistance of a terrestrial station. All terrestrial users attempt to collect a sufficient number of Fountain packets to reconstruct the desired data. We derive exact expressions of outage probability (OP) of two clusters and system OP (SOP), and then conduct simulations to verify this expression. This paper also investigates the impact of power allocation factors on the OP and SOP performance.

articleTitle: ETA: Enriching Typos Automatically from Real-World Corpora for Few-Shot Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Spell checking is the task of rectifying errors in a sentence resulting from various factors, and despite continuous research in this field, research often focused on widely known specific languages, such as English and Chinese. In this study, we focus on the Korean language and its linguistic features, particularly the propensity for a single character can be incorrect in diverse ways. Therefore, we categorize spelling errors from real-world corpora and automatically construct an error corpus based on their statistical patterns. When we employed them to leverage the impact of a pretrained large language model (LLM), we confirmed that utilizing the introduced spelling errors as samples for few-shot learning can be helpful in error correction tasks. We hope that this study contributes to the automatic construction of error corpora and prompt-based approaches for providing a better quality of consumer service, especially provoke research related to other low-resource languages in spell checking tasks.

articleTitle: Accuracy Simulation of MF R-Mode Systems Using TOA Variance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: To ensure consistent navigation services despite GNSS signal disruptions, Korea is developing the R-Mode system. This study focuses on enhancing the simulation accuracy of the MF R-Mode system's performance by integrating data from the Eocheong transmitter with existing data from the Palmi and Chungju transmitters. Additional measurements from these three transmitters were gathered using the DARBS receiver to model the Time-of-Arrival (TOA) variance. Analysis of this data facilitated the calculation of new constants and transmitter-specific jitter values, which were then used to determine coverage areas based on the updated parameters.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of the Dual-Hop Satellite-Terrestrial Network with Imperfect CSI and Direct Link
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper presents an analysis of the performance of hybrid satellite-terrestrial relaying (HSTR) networks with user selection schemes. Specifically, we investigate the outage probability of the HSTR networks while accounting for the direct link and imperfect channel state information (CSI). Three user selection schemes are considered: direct link-based, indirect link-based, and end-to-end (e2e) based schemes. In the direct link-based scheme, the best user is selected based on the direct link's quality. The indirect link-based scheme selects the best user via the relay, while the end-to-end based scheme combines both links using selection combining techniques at the user. Numerical computations are provided to identify the most effective selection scheme and to highlight the impact of key parameters on performance metrics.

articleTitle: Direct Time-of-Flight Sensor System Based on SPAD IC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In recent years, direct time-of-flight (dToF) sensor systems have become crucial in autonomous vehicles, light detection and ranging (LiDAR), and 3D imaging applications. Single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs), highly-sensitive detectors capable of capturing individual photons, play a vital role in the systems by enabling high-resolution imaging and accurate distance measurement. Time-to-digital converters (TDCs) are crucial for dToF systems as they allow for high-precision, picosecond-level measurements by converting time intervals into digital values. In this paper, we present the design of TDC using a voltage-controlled Vernier delay line. We also show simulation results of the dToF system, which include the analog front-end (AFE) for the SPAD, TDC, and FPGA-based histogram, using a Verilog-A SPAD model based on SPAD's characteristics.

articleTitle: Evaluating Deep Learning Models for Prediction of Climate Conditions in Greenhouse
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of four representative deep learning models-1D CNN (Convolutional Neural Network), LSTM (Long-Short Term Memory), DNN (Deep Neural Network), and Transformer-for environmental prediction in smart greenhouses using 13 sensing data. Data collected at one-minute intervals over nine months were used to compare the prediction performance for temperature, humidity, and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> levels at three different time intervals (5 minutes, 30 minutes, and 60 minutes). The results showed that prediction errors increased as the time interval grew larger. Predictions within 30 minutes were deemed applicable for complex environmental control in smart farm systems, while predictions for 60 minutes ahead could be used to forecast general trends. This approach can support more precise environmental control through proactive predictive management in smart greenhouses.

articleTitle: Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Empathetic Dialogue: An Integrated Approach Using Speech and Text
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: With the advancement of computer performance and the progress in machine learning and natural language processing technologies, interactive AI systems capable of dialog with humans have emerged. However, in achieving truly human-like interaction, the ability to understand human emotions and exhibit appropriate empathetic responses, rather than merely providing logical replies, is still room for improvement. In this study, we have constructed models using Japanese empathetic spoken dialog corpus that includes empathetic conversations. We have developed models that utilize speech features, text features, and a multimodal model that integrates both. Comparing the accuracy of each model, the speech model achieved 0.752, the text model achieved 0.704, and the multimodal model achieved 0.813, with the multimodal model demonstrating the highest accuracy. By comparing the accuracy of each model by emotion, we have identified which model is more effective in recognizing specific emotions and demonstrated that the multimodal model effectively captures diverse data features, contributing to improved accuracy.

articleTitle: MACeIP: A Multimodal Ambient Context-Enriched Intelligence Platform in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a Multimodal Ambient Context-enriched Intelligence Platform (MACeIP) for Smart Cities, a comprehensive system designed to enhance urban management and citizen engagement. Our platform integrates advanced technologies, including Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, edge and cloud computing, and Multimodal AI, to create a responsive and intelligent urban ecosystem. Key components include Interactive Hubs for citizen interaction, an extensive IoT sensor network, intelligent public asset management, a pedestrian monitoring system, a City Planning Portal, and a Cloud Computing System. We demonstrate the prototype of MACeIP in several cities, focusing on Fredericton, New Brunswick. This work contributes to innovative city development by offering a scalable, efficient, and user-centric approach to urban intelligence and management.

articleTitle: A Survey of Unsupervised Learning-Based Out-of-Distribution Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection is the task of distinguishing abnormal data that lies outside the bounds of the training dataset's distribution. OOD detection plays a vital role in various applications of machine learning and deep learning, including intrusion detection in cybersecurity, diagnostics in med-ical data, and defect classification in manufacturing processes. While models for OOD detection are typically trained using supervised learning, this approach requires significant cost and effort such as collection and labeling of OOD data. To address this issue, unsupervised learning-based methods have been proposed, which can overcome the drawbacks of supervised approaches. In this paper, we introduce generative model-based OOD methods and self-supervised OOD detection methods within the realm of unsupervised learning. We also analyze the performance of state-of-the-art unsupervised learning-based OOD methods to suggest future research directions.

articleTitle: Enhancing Training Speed and Stability Through Symmetry in Diffusion Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Diffusion model has achieved great success in generative models, but they require significant time and data to train. Furthermore, the training of the diffusion model can be unstable or fail to converge, especially when using an inappropriate learning rate with limited GPU capacity. We suggest a Symmetrize Noise Sampling (SNS) method to achieve faster and more stable convergence of the diffusion models especially in limited computing environments. This method guarantees that the mean of the noise sampled from the Gaussian distribution used to train the diffusion model is always zero, thereby ensuring that the mathematical assumptions of the diffusion model are strictly adhered to throughout the training process. The experimental results have validated the effectiveness of our method on training of a diffusion model.

articleTitle: Presentation of Position and Relative Speed of Surrounding Vehicles by Tactile Stimuli to Upper Limb
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The visual load on drivers has recently increased owing to an increase in the amount of information provided by more sophisticated functions and larger displays. Presenting non-visual information could help reduce the load on the drivers. This study focuses on the presentation of spatial information by tactile stimuli to the upper limb, proposing that the position of surrounding vehicles is shown as an extension of the direction of the vibration position from the eye point to the upper limb. The relative speed of the passing vehicles is then perceived by the difference in travel time between the sites of stimulation to the upper limb. The relationship between the physical and perceived angle of vibration position from the eye point to the upper limb was first investigated. The difference in travel time between the sites of stimulation to the upper limb was then tested to verify whether relative speed could be perceived, and the feasibility of the tactile presentation system was confirmed. The results revealed a strong correlation between the physical and perceived angles. The difference in speed could be recognized with high probability. The acceptability of this system was evaluated, resulting in a score of 2.44 on a 5-point scale from 0 to 4, indicating a relatively positive response.

articleTitle: A Compact Planar Branch-Line Hybrid Coupler for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper presents a planar branch-line hybrid coupler with the characteristic of broadband. The frequency range for operating is improved by making consecutive resonators through using two sections. In addition, the compactness is achieved thanks to using zigzag lines. Based on RogerRT/Duroid 5870 substrate layer <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{h}=0.7874$</tex> mm, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}=2.33$</tex>, tanδ = 0.0012), the final design witnesses a total dimension of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.37 \lambda_0 \times 10.34 \lambda_0 \times x 0.0057\lambda_0$</tex>, in which <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\lambda_0$</tex> is the free-space wavelength at the lowest operating frequency of 2.2 GHz and the bandwidth percentage of 49% at S11 under -10 dB and the isolation of more than 15 dB.

articleTitle: Matrix Accelerator Designed for Vision Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Due to the popularity of large language models such as Generative Pre-Trained Transformer (GPT), many researchers have invested in the research of the Transformer model. Vision Transformer has become one of the most popular research directions in the field of computer vision. Different from the previous Convolutional Neural Network, Vision Transformer blocks the image and adopts Self-Attention. The model can capture the information in the image globally, not just local features. However, a large number of matrix operations consume a lot of GPU resources and memory space. The goal of this paper is to design a dedicated chip to support the digital storage and processing of images. The goal is to design based on the Vision Transformer architecture, focusing on the implementation of matrix multiplication and Softmax of Attention in the Encoder. The completed circuit is simulated running at a clock frequency of 100MHz. Compared with CPU hardware acceleration, the running speed is 51.5 times faster.

articleTitle: Extraordinary Optical Transmission Biosensor for Rapid Hypoalbuminemia Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Hypoalbuminemia, marked by low blood albumin levels, indicates various diseases and requires swift, accurate diagnostics. We developed a diagnostic kit with an Extraordinary Optical Transmission (EOT) biosensor for rapid, precise albumin measurement. Using nanohole arrays, the EOT sensor showed a 460 nm/RIU sensitivity and detected albumin as low as 10 mg/mL with a 0.8972 nm peak shift. It accurately classified 100 serum samples with over 98% accuracy. This kit provides a promising real-time, label-free diagnostic solution, particularly with advanced microfluidics and thin-film optics.

articleTitle: Local Binary Patterns for Classifying Pistachio Species
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: To maintain the economic value of pistachio nuts, which is vital in the agricultural economy, efficient post-harvest industrial processes are essential. Different pistachio species cater to distinct markets, increasing the need for accurate classification methods. This study introduces an alternative feature extraction approach using Local Binary Pattern (LBP) to enhance the classification of pistachio species. We apply this method to a dataset comprising 2,148 images of two pistachio species, Kirmizi and Siirt, each with unique market-relevant characteristics. Various machine learning models are evaluated, with Multilayer Perceptron (MLP) emerging as the most effective, achieving a classification accuracy of 96.74%. The findings demonstrate that machine learning methods, combined with LBP, significantly improve the performance and efficiency of pistachio variety classification. These results hold promising applications in precise pistachio selection and intelligent farming techniques.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement for Rateless Codes-Aided Hybrid Satellite-Terrestrial Multi-User Networks Using NOMA and IRS With Presence of Multiple Eavesdroppers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes a rateless code (RC) aided hybrid satellite-terrestrial relaying (HSTR) multi-user scheme using non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA) and intelligent reflecting surface (IRS), with the presence of multiple eavesdroppers. In our scheme, a satellite uses NOMA to transmit two RC packets to a terrestrial station that relays the received packets to two ground users, with the help of IRS. Two ground users and the eavesdroppers attempt to sufficiently collect number of RC packets before the transmission ends. This paper measures outage performance and intercept performance of the proposed scheme via analysis and simulations. We also investigate the effect of important parameters on the performance.

articleTitle: The Novel Image Sensor with Inverter Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This study examines the performance of an NMOS inverter-based image sensor circuit. Simulation results show that as the input voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{i} \mathbf{n}}\right)$</tex> increases from 4V to 5V, the output voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\left(\mathbf{V}_{{\mathbf{o}\mathbf{u}\mathbf{t} }}\right)$</tex> drops sharply from 9.41V to 2.74V, highlighting the circuit's precise voltage transfer characteristics. Additionally, variations in the transistor threshold voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{t}\mathbf{h}})$</tex> I, specifically adjusting Vth to 0.2V and 1.2V, have minimal impact on the output voltage, demonstrating the circuit's stability. The nonlinear response of the output voltage to changes in the input voltage indicates a high level of sensitivity. Overall, the proposed circuit exhibits both high precision and stability, suggesting that further performance improvements could be achieved through design optimization.

articleTitle: Condition-Based Monitoring for Failure Detection and Cause Identification in Wafer Transfer Robot Using Machine Learning and Explainable Artificial Intelligence Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This study introduces a method for real-time prediction of failures in Wafer Transfer Robot (WTR), which is critical in semiconductor manufacturing. Using data from acceleration sensors and fast Fourier transformation (FFT) for anomaly detection, the approach involves modeling failure data for high-risk components like bearing motor, ball screw, timing belt, robot hand, and end effector. A deep neural network (DNN) differentiates between normal and failure states, and a random forest (RF) algorithm classifies the failure components. Additionally, the Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) algorithm pinpoints the frequency bands liked to specific failure causes, enhancing the identification of failure causes in WTR.

articleTitle: Normal-Adaptive Memory Module for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Weakly-Supervised Video Anomaly Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Video Anomaly Detection (VAD) effectively identifies abnormal events in surveillance systems, utilizing both temporal intervals and pixel-level analysis. However, due to the domain gap between datasets, current VAD approaches are only effective in the in-domain context. These issues hinder adaptation and generalization across multiple source datasets, leading to inadequate detection of abnormal events. To address these challenges, we propose a Domain-adaptive Memory Module (DAMM) designed to utilize across various domains. This module facilitates the definition of normalcy and allows for easy adaptation through unsupervised methods in unseen domains. Our method demonstrates superior performance in VAD tasks, achieving significant results across two benchmark datasets.

articleTitle: Achieving Stable Handover Delays in LTE Railway Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The stable A3 offset control for the stabilized average handover delay was proposed and the performance was evaluated by the OPNET network simulator. in the paper. The LTE railway system typically requires the short inter-cell site distance (ISD) in order to high safety and reliable wireless control, so that the stable handover delay against frequent handover is essential to wireless remote train control system design. The performance relative to handover delay was analyzed at train speeds of 50 and 100 km/h. The average handover delay was mostly affected by variation of A3 offset values as mentioned in the simulation results. It means that the stable average handover delay by adjusting A3 offsets can be achieved. The results showed us that there were unstable and stable region to average handover delay in terms of RSRP and RSRQ regarding variation of A3 offset values. In this way, we can achieve the stable and predictable average handover delay for wireless remote train control system by controlling them in the stable region.

articleTitle: Optical and Electrical Characterization of Single-Photon Avalanche Diodes Fabricated in CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper presents the design, fabrication, and characterization of single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) fabricated in 110 nm CMOS technology, optimized for photon-counting imaging and LiDAR applications. The SPADs are designed with active region sizes of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5 \mu ~\mathrm{m}, 10 \mu ~\mathrm{m}, 15 \mu ~\mathrm{m}$</tex>, and 20 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, and feature a retrograde virtual guard-ring (GR) structure to prevent premature edge breakdown. Electrical and optical characteristics, including current-voltage (I-V) curve, dark count rate (DCR), and photon detection probability (PDP), were measured to evaluate the performance of SPADs.

articleTitle: Low Power Offset-Tolerant Sense Amplifier Using Dynamic Boosting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This study proposes a dynamically boosted sample-boost-latch sense amplifier (DSBLSA). The use of dynamic boosting makes the circuit more offset-tolerant and allows operation at 70-80% energy consumption for identical performance. Additionally, this paper also proposes a scheme to maximize the dynamic boosting. The proposed circuit was validated via HSPICE simulations using a 28-nm CMOS PDK.

articleTitle: A Reinforcement Learning-Based Computational Model of Human Elbow Joint Operation for Effective Human-Machine Interface
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Designing effective human-machine interfaces requires understanding complex interactions between humans and machines. However, even bi-directional communication that relies on sensor data is often insufficient due to the unpredictability of human behaviors. To better anticipate these behaviors, a computational model that reflects the operating principles of the human nervous system is essential. This study presents a computational neuromechanical model that focuses on human sensorimotor operations, particularly in the context of elbow joint rotation. The model leverages reinforcement learning (RL) to simulate the brain's reward mechanism in motor adjustment, with the reward function adjusted by a multiplication constant (M) that reflects individual variability in sensorimotor processing. Measurement and simulation data were evaluated based on their overlap ratios. The test results demonstrate that the RL-based model, when calibrated with an optimal M value, closely matches with measured motor outputs, indicating its potential for improving the effectiveness of the human-machine interface.

articleTitle: Entropy-Guided Head Importance for Token Pruning in Vision Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: To address the challenges posed by the high computational load of Vision Transformers, various lightweight methods such as pruning and quantization have been proposed. Among them, token pruning aims to reduce the overall computational load of Vision Transformers by assessing the importance of each token, which is the computational unit, and excluding or reducing computations for tokens with lower importance. To minimize accuracy loss due to token pruning, it is crucial to accurately select the important tokens. In this paper, we propose an entropy guided head importance method for token pruning to achieve this goal.

articleTitle: A Proposal of the Gamification of Programming Learning Assistant System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Despite the rapid expansion of the ICT sector, there's a disconnect with STEM subjects, leading to high dropout rates in computer science and engineering programs. This contributes to many unfilled positions in the ICT job market. One key issue is that traditional teaching methods struggle to engage students in challenging and abstract STEM subjects like programming. To address this, innovative technology-enhanced learning solutions are needed to be developed. In the past, we have developed a Programming Learning Assistant System (PLAS) to support programming learning for novice students. PLAS offers several types of exercise problems to foster code reading and writing skills at different levels. In this paper, we propose the initial prototype of the gamification of PLAS to enhance students' comprehension of programming concepts, improve their confidence, cultivate their interest in STEM fields, and increase course engagement through dynamic and engaing scenarios.

articleTitle: Biomolecular Detection Based on Surface Enhanced Raman Scattering with Dielectrophoretic Manipulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Plasmonic nanoarrays were used to localize surface plasmon for surface-enhanced acquisition of Raman signatures. To selectively capture and enhance Raman signals of the surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) system, we combine precise manipulation of target particles based on dielectrophoresis (DEP).
