Our system integrates metal nanostructures with interdigitated microelectrodes to enable the evaluation of the electrophysiological properties of microparticles. By modulating the frequency of the applied alternating current field, we can control particle movement based on their electrical characteristics, such as conductivity and permittivity. For the proof-of-concept, we have measured polystyrene (PS) beads as well as biological cells (U-87MG cell-line). Within this integrated system, SERS was performed with significantly increased efficiency. The real-time measurement of enhanced Raman scattering was achieved by dynamically controlling the force direction on individual particles, allowing us to selectively trap them on the nanostructured surfaces for analysis.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Based Beam Training for Extremely Large-Scale MIMO Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: We propose a deep learning-based beam training method for extremely large-scale multiple-input multiple-output (XL-MIMO) systems. This method addresses the challenge of increased beam training overhead in near-field environments by activating specific subsets of the antenna array. Using beam gain measurements from an angular codebook, we train a deep learning model to select the optimal codeword from a hybrid codebook that incorporates near-field and far-field scenarios. Simulation results demonstrate that our approach improves normalized beam gain and data rate while significantly reducing the beam training overhead.

articleTitle: Secrecy Performance Analysis of RF Energy Harvesting UAV-Enabled NOMA MEC System Under Eavesdropping Scenario
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper investigates a radio frequency (RF) energy harvesting (EH) non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-aided mobile edge computing (MEC) network with one legitimate unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), one eavesdropping UAV and dual computing access points (APs), in which NOMA technology is applied to transmit workload data streams to APs for computing. Besides, an AP, known as a hybrid AP (HAP), supports a radio power supply service for UAV. To measure the performance of the considered NOMA-aided MEC UAV network, we first developed the four-phase system protocol to ensure delay and security capabilities. Accordingly, we analyze system performance using the secrecy successful computation probability (SSCP) metric. Finally, we conduct experiments to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system and compare our numerical results with Monte-Carlo simulations, finding excellent agreement.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Hip Muscle Activation and Gait Kinematics During Motorized and Self-Propelled Treadmill Walking
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Hip muscles play a vital role in maintaining balance and proper gait, and treadmill walking is one of the most popular ways to train hip muscles by cyclic movement of the lower limb. However, the effectiveness of treadmill walking for hip muscle training remains unclear, due to insufficient data on hip muscle activity during treadmill walking. This study provides a comparative analysis of hip muscle activity and gait kinematics during motorized and self-propelled treadmill walking. Using a wireless electromyography (EMG) device and motion capture system, we evaluated hip muscle activity and gait kinematics. Our results indicate that the selfpropelled treadmill walking demands greater hip muscle activation than the motorized counterpart, as evidenced by elevated EMG activity, which is likely required to maintain gait stability and generate forward propulsion without external assistance. Furthermore, participants demonstrated increased step length during self-propelled treadmill walking, suggesting an adaptation to the absence of the external assistance, though gait symmetry remained unaffected. Most importantly, selfpropelled treadmill walking necessitated greater hip flexion, emphasizing its potential for enhancing hip muscle engagement in treadmill exercise. These findings underscore the importance of incorporating self-propelled treadmill walking into the exercise routine for hip muscle training, particularly for the gluteal muscle development.

articleTitle: Generative Adversarial Network-Based Network Intrusion Detection System for Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In the context of burgeoning cyber threats targeting Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems, this paper presents a pioneering Intrusion Detection System (IDS) grounded in Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). The ubiquity of information technology in critical industrial processes necessitates heightened security measures, and the proposed model addresses this imperative through the fusion of GANs and IDS tailored for SCADA environments. The study delves into the evolutionary trajectory of Intrusion Detection Systems, tracing their progression from conventional signature-based methods to the adaptive capabilities afforded by artificial intelligence, particularly deep learning. Against this backdrop, the paper investigates the vulnerabilities of SCADA systems, elucidating the sophisticated attack vectors identified in recent studies. The distributed nature of SCADA systems, deployed across extensive industrial landscapes, accentuates the need for robust intrusion detection mechanisms. This research's core innovation lies in applying a GAN model to SCADA systems, leveraging the distributed network protocol version 3 (DNP3) for data access authorization. The model is trained on a dataset comprising 12 meticulously selected features from DNP3 packets, attuning it to the nuances of SCADA network traffic. Notably, the proposed GAN-based IDS demonstrates exceptional efficacy, achieving impressive accuracy. Beyond the empirical contributions, the paper envisions future directions for integrating explainable AI techniques and enhancing the interpretability of IDS models specific to SCADA environments. Moreover, collaboration between academia and industry is advocated to foster the development of comprehensive datasets that represent SCADA network traffic.

articleTitle: Enhancing Survivor Localization Performance Using Residual U-Net for Interference Cancellation in Disaster Situations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper introduces a method to improve the accuracy of detecting and locating individuals in disaster situations with interference signals. The approach features an interference cancellation model that isolates and refines the rescue request signal, enhancing input quality for the localization model. The localization uses the generalized cross-correlation phase transform (GCC-PHAT) technique to estimate sound source positions. In interference-free conditions, the model achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 1.16 meters and a Euclidean distance (ED) error of 0.89 meters. However, in 0 dB SNR environments, the MAE worsens to 2.35 meters and the ED to 1.88 meters. With the interference cancellation model, the system improves, reducing the MAE to 1.81 meters and the ED to 1.43 meters under the same conditions. These results demonstrate the model's effectiveness in mitigating noise effects, enhancing survivor detection and localization accuracy, critical for timely rescue operations.

articleTitle: X-Band GaN Power Amplifier MMIC Design and Radiation Evaluations for Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper reports on the development of X-band GaN power amplifier (PA) monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) that is suitable for active electronically scanned array (AESA) radar and satellite synthetic aperture radar (SAR) applications. The PA MMIC designed using GH15-10 GaN technology exhibits gain of 27 dB, output power of 42.5 dBm, and PAE of 55 % in the 8.5~11 GHz frequency range with a compact size of 3.78 mm × 1.3 mm. Also, radiation evaluations with TID and SEE tests of the developed MMIC are discussed.

articleTitle: Latency and Secrecy Performance Analysis in Backscatter-Enabled Vehicular Cloudlet Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In this work, we investigate the joint secrecy and latency performance of a multi-user backscatter communication (BC)-enabled vehicular network in the presence of a passive eavesdropper. Specifically, a number of vehicles intend to offload their tasks to a vehicle equipped with a mobile edge computing (MEC) server by utilizing dedicated BC communication and time division multiple access (TDMA) schemes. Meanwhile, a passive mobile eavesdropper attempts to intercept information from each user without any attacks. In order to investigate the performance of this system, we derive the closed-form expressions of the successful computation probability (SCP) and secrecy successful computation probability (SSCP) in two corresponding scenarios: with and without eavesdropper. In addition, the impacts of key parameters on the system's behavior to gain insight into its performance are also examined. Finally, the numerical results using Monte-Carlo simulations are provided to validate our analysis.

articleTitle: Text-Image Data Classification and Cross-Modal Retrieval Method Using Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In this paper, we present a text-image data classification and cross-modal retrieval method using feature fusion. Features from various data types are obtained by extracting their embedding vector through multiple encoders. A contrastive learning process is added while training the network to make different features similar. The extracted features are generated as high-quality fused features through cross-attention of the transformer. The proposed method is evaluated, and it shows that text-image data classification performance was higher than the method using a single data type. We also confirmed that the cross-modal retrieval method using the image and text encoders of the trained network showed high performance.

articleTitle: Human Perception on Weight in Networked Virtual Environment with Haptic Sense
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In this paper, to improve the efficiency of QoS control, we developed a networked golden dolphin system with haptic feedback and an AI server that provides optimal parameters for QoS control based on data training. As the first step in our research, we aim to clarify the relationship between weight perception, which is a crucial parameter for QoS control, by experiment. In our experiment, each user is asked to lift a golden dolphin and determine whether the weight has changed when adjustments are made. We also vary the size of the golden dolphin to examine whether human perception is influenced by the object's size. The experimental results show that all subjects can perceive weight changes when the difference is larger than about 40 gf.

articleTitle: Map Presentation in Walking Support System With Wearable Sensors by Metaverse
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper proposes to add a function to a metaverse-based walking support system that presents a map of the metaverse and indicates the current position and goal position on the map. Users can move in the metaverse space by wearing wearable sensors (e.g., ankle and waist sensors) and performing a stepping motion and dynamically change the speed of movement according to the stepping speed. The added function would encourage the stepping motion in the elderly because it would tell the user how far he/she need to walk from the current position to the goal position.

articleTitle: Advancing Medical Diagnostics: Performance Analysis of YOLO Algorithms for Automated Platelet Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The significance of health automation, particularly post-COVID-19, emphasizes the critical role of advanced diagnostic technologies. Conventional methods for platelet detection in blood-smear images are often slow and inconsistent, impacting medical response efficiency. This study explores the application of the YOLO (You Only Look Once) algorithm, specifically versions 3, 5, 7, and 8, to improve platelet detection accuracy and efficiency. Through meticulous data preparation and fine-tuning on a curated dataset, we compared the performance of these YOLO versions in terms of accuracy, precision, recall, and computational efficiency. YOLOv5 emerged as the most accurate and reliable model, achieving the highest mean Average Precision (mAP) and superior precision and recall metrics, despite slightly slower inference times compared to YOLOv8. YOLOv8, with the fastest inference times and excellent detection capabilities, is also highly effective for real-time applications. The findings underscore the advancements and tradeoffs among different YOLO versions, with YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 showing significant potential for enhancing automated platelet detection in clinical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Mixed Traffic Flow Modeling Solution on Digital Map
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced mixed traffic flow modeling solution utilizing deep learning and computer vision techniques integrated with digital mapping technologies. The proposed system employs YOLOv8 to detect and classify various traffic participants, including cars, trucks,… DeepSORT for multi-object tracking. OpenCV, along with our specialized algorithms, is utilized to estimate the speed of each detected object, recognize vehicle license plates, and determine the GPS location of each participant based on the camera's geolocation. These data points are then used to simulate real-time traffic flow on a digital map. The system's effectiveness is validated through a series of experiments, demonstrating its potential for digitizing traffic flow on a digital map, thereby enhancing traffic management and urban planning.

articleTitle: Electro-Optic Effect of the Optical Switch Panel Using Liquid Crystal Nanocapsules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This study presents the development and characterization of optical switch panels utilizing nanosized liquid crystal (LC) capsules, approximately 200 nm in diameter. These capsules, composed of a nematic host LC and dichroic dyes, were fabricated using a coacervation method. The process involved forming thin polymeric shells around the LC droplets, which were then chemically crosslinked for enhanced stability. The panels were constructed by printing the LC capsules between two ITO-coated PET substrates, with a liquid crystal layer thickness of 15 μm, The electro-optic performance of the panels was evaluated by measuring the transmittance under varying applied voltages and dye concentrations. The results demonstrate that the alignment of LC molecules and dichroic dyes within the nanosized capsules significantly modulates light transmission, offering improved optical switching capabilities. This research contributes to advancing the design and application of nanoscale LC-based optical switches in display technologies.

articleTitle: IEEE 802.11ah Throughput Measurement with Real Devices in Forest for High Speed Forest Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: We evaluate IEEE802.11ah communication quality in the forests in mountain areas, mainly for video communications. Compared with Wi-Fi or IEEE802.11ax, IEEE802.11ah can cover a larger area but obtain lower transmission speed or throughput. In a forest, many trees, branches, and leaves can be obstacles to radio waves as NLOS (Non-Line of Sight), but the signal attenuation level depends on the density of such obstacles. We used real devices of IEEE802.11ah of consumer markets on the experiments in areal forest for various distance between the devices. IEEE802.11ah devices showed their quality of service of communication at around 230 meters distance with more than 2.5 Mbps throughput, which is enough for video conferencing or 720p video streaming.

articleTitle: A Low Power Attention and Softmax Accelerator for Large Language Models Inference
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Transformer-based models, essential for high-performing Large Language Models (LLMs), surpass traditional Deep Neural Networks but require substantial computational resources. Therefore, more efficient transformer algorithms and accelerators are required to reduce the computational cost and power consumption of LLMs. We observed that as the sequence length increases, softmax operations, which are the key operation of the transformer self-attention mechanism, become the major bottleneck. In this paper, we propose Cross-Road Softmax, an optimized algorithm designed for the softmax operation within the attention layer, specifically tailored for inference in LLMs. Our software experiment was conducted on 8 Natural Language Processing benchmarks for evaluation. Furthermore, we design a Cross-Road Accel using the proposed Cross-Road Softmax that accelerates softmax function of the self-attention layer. We implement Cross-Road Accel in RTL and synthesize it with Syn-opsys Design Compiler using Nangate 15nm open cell library to obtain power and area statistics. In summary, on average, Cross-Road Accel achieves an approximately 3.5 × increase in energy efficiency compared to state-of-the-art transformer accelerators.

articleTitle: Efficient Image Alignment Scheme for Automated Optical Inspection of Printed Circuit Boards
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper investigates the application of automated optical inspection (ADI) in determining missing and incorrect components in printed circuit boards (PCBs) during the production line. Instead of employing computationally intensive CNN models, we adopt a simple image registration and matching based scheme. Despite of its simplicity, precise image alignment with the reference image of a flawless PCB is crucial to the inspection accuracy. Image alignment should overcome the impacts of camera shooting angles and the positional and angular deviations of the captured PCB image. A two-stage approach consisting of a coarse positioning and a fine calibration is developed. In stage 1, the reference image is first partitioned into inspection blocks and a Normalized Cross-Correlation (NCC) scheme is used to find the most similar blocks in the target image. In stage 2, feature points extraction and matching are performed under an iterative RANSAC (Random Sample Consensus) framework. Finally, a homography matrix is derived for fine calibration. Experimental results show that the alignment can be completed in 118.6ms and the average alignment error is less than 5 pixels.

articleTitle: Enhanced Electrical Performance in SiC Double-Trench MOSFETs through Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Single-trench SiC MOSFETs structures offer lower on-resistance but reduce the breakdown voltage. To overcome this limitation, double-trench SiC power MOSFETs have been developed. In this study, Baliga's Figure of Merit (BFOM) was improved by adjusting the drift region doping concentration, as well as the depth and angle of the source trench. The simulation results demonstrate that as the doping concentration in the drift region increases, the BFOM reaches its peak at a value of 1.02GW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> when the doping concentration in the drift region is 4 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, before subsequently decreasing. Additionally, increasing the source trench depth to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.8 \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> shifts the doping concentration at which the BFOM reaches its maximum to 6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>, resulting in an improved BFOM of 2.4GW/cm2. When the source trench angle is adjusted to 94 degrees, with a doping concentration of 6 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">15</sup> cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>and a source trench depth of 1.8 μm, the BFOM further increases to 2.72GW/cm2.

articleTitle: Blockchain-Based Key State Management for IoT Devices in Post-Quantum Era
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Blockchain has been paving the way for new business opportunities as we have witnessed over the last few years. It will continue to proliferate further and be adopted in increasingly diverse sectors. One area of research in Blockchain is how it can be used in Internet of Things (IoT) based applications like Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV), Smart cities and Healthcare. However, with the advent of quantum technology, some widely used security algorithms in blockchain are vulnerable (i.e., quantum algorithms can exponentially solve cryptographic algorithms used to digitally sign or encrypt data), thereby diminishing communication security. Thus, post-quantum algorithms are at the forefront of research to secure data before quantum technologies can fully mature. Early standardized post-quantum algorithms such as hash-based one-time signatures, relies on the proven one-way-ness of hashing algorithm. Hash-based one-time signatures require robust secret key management systems to prevent security degradation. To safeguard IoT applications from quantum threats, this paper proposes a solution which utilizes both hash-based one-time signatures and blockchain to cover each technology's weaknesses.

articleTitle: Commercial-Off-the-Shelf Force Feedback System to Enhance Teleoperation Control Accuracy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Teleoperation systems are essential for task completion in challenging or hazardous environments where unmanned operation is necessary. A significant limitation of the current teleoperation system is the lack of cost-effective solutions that provide precise force feedback, which is crucial for accurate and intuitive control. This study presents a real-time force feedback system using easily accessible commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) components and demonstrates that the presented force feedback system enhances the operator's control accuracy in teleoperation. The presented system utilizes flex and force sensors installed over the gloves and the robotic gripper, respectively, along with a microcontroller that translates finger movements into gripper actions and provides force feedback to the operator's fingers. Six healthy human subjects participated in the experiment, performing manipulation tasks under two feedback conditions: vision-only and vision with force feedback. Test results demonstrated that the inclusion of force feedback reduced the initial contact force by approximately 40% in scenarios where visual information was limited. These findings confirm the effectiveness of the presented COTS system in delivering force feedback and improving control accuracy in teleoperation tasks.

articleTitle: Impact of Target Speech Length on Performance in Voice Conversion Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: In voice conversion (VC), which transforms acoustic characteristics of one voice (source speech) to another (target speech), it is essential to preserve the linguistic content of the source speech while accurately extracting style information from the target speech. However, in existing deep learning-based vc frameworks, introducing short target speech results in less reliable style extraction, leading to decreased performance. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the conversion performance of three state-of-the-art vc models with different network architectures, focusing on the impact of target speech duration. Our experiments demonstrate the impact of target speech length on speaker similarity and linguistic content intelli-gibility. Absolute scores and their variability differ depending on the specific neural frameworks of the vc models. These findings provide valuable insights for designing vc systems for applications with limited target speech duration.

articleTitle: BlazeGuard: An Automated Fire Prevention Plug for Electronics and Appliances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The leading cause of home fires is appliance and battery fires, where devices get extremely hot and typically produce smoke before catching fire. These fires can be prevented if devices can be shut off when high heat or smoke can be detected before a fire starts. This paper presents the design and implementation of BlazeGuard, a smart plug, capable of being used with any existing outlets which can enable the user to plug in any devices or appliances. These plugs will be able to automatically monitor current, detect heat, smoke, and voltage usage using onboard sensors. To adapt to various devices/appliances they will include a module with external sensors for situations where the outlet is far away from the device in question. If anyone of these parameters nears concerning levels the device will shut off power to that device and alert the user. BlazeGuard will also have the ability to cut off power after a time limit to prevent overcharging on devices without that protection and offer real time alerts to the user. Contrary to current solutions which require extensive rewiring, and offer only certain features, BlazeGuard provides a cost effective and reliable solution to fire prevention.

articleTitle: Efficient Directed Controller Synthesis Using Action Priority
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Discrete Controller Synthesis is a technology designed to automatically synthesize controllers that ensure safety in predefined environmental conditions. Discrete Controller Syn-thesis generates these controllers from environment models and monitoring models, which are represented by Labeled Transition Systems. A significant challenge arises from the fact that the state space, which models the entire environment, grows exponentially with the number of environment models, leading to a corresponding exponential increase in computational space in Discrete Controller Synthesis approaches that construct the complete model. To address this, Directed Controller Synthesis (DCS) has been developed, utilizing on-the-fly exploration to mitigate the expansive state space issue. However, DCS faces challenges with computation time, which heavily depends on the exploration strategy, and current strategies are potentially inefficient, often resulting in prolonged synthesis times for controllers. Therefore, this study proposes Directed Controller Synthesis Using Action Priority(DSCAP), which improves the exploration efficiency of DCS by incorporating action priority.

articleTitle: Prognosis Analysis for Ovarian Cancer Patients Using Protein Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Ovarian cancer is one of the most common genetic diseases caused by genetic mutations or chromosomal abnormal-ities. In the research field, many researchers have made efforts to identify cancer biomarkers using various genomic approaches. However, genomic changes are not the only factors that determine the phenotype of cancer cells, as millions of various factors are expressed in ovarian cancer. Therefore, there is a problem that research on identifying symptoms in cancer patients based on data is insufficient. To solve this problem, we propose a key factor selection technique based on unsupervised learning as well as a novel data preprocessing technique suitable for medical data with a large number of features. By applying this method, it is possible to select protein factors that could diagnose the patient's prognosis. Also, the effectiveness of the proposed technique is proven based on the TMA cohort process. With the proposed method, it is possible to indirectly analyze the prognosis of cancer patients and apply customized treatment methods for each patient. Furthermore, we could implement solutions and products that could periodically monitor the patient's condition.

articleTitle: DoNaAI: Deep Learning-Based Ensemble Approach for Waste Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Effective solid waste management is crucial in Vietnam due to rapid urbanization. This article presents an AI-based approach to improve waste classification using deep learning models like ResNet, MobileNet, and DenseNet. Trained on ViWaste, a dataset of 10,000 waste images, and enhanced with data augmentation techniques, these models achieved high accuracy in waste classification. Based on these findings, a complete application was developed to support efficient recycling operations. The study demonstrates the potential of deep learning models in promoting environmental sustainability and its broader integration into waste management in developing regions.

articleTitle: Micro LED Pixel Circuit with Threshold Voltage Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: The display is applied to many electronic products such as computers, smartphones, and TVs. In particular, Micro LEDs are evaluated as one of the next-generation displays and many studies are currently underway. This study examines a micro pixel circuit featuring a-IGZO TFT, incorporating a PWM method that adjusts pulse width based on the signal magnitude. And it aims not only to compensate for the threshold voltage but also to improve the inrush current phenomenon. When the threshold voltages of the two drive transistors in the previously proposed pixel circuit vary, the error rate values were from 0.015% to 0.90%. When the threshold voltages of two driving TFTs of the proposed pixel circuit, change, the error rate values came out from 0.053% to 0.144%. Finally, the simulation results confirmed that not only the threshold voltage compensation but also the inrush current phenomenon was improved through the proposed pixel circuit.

articleTitle: NOMA-Aided Cell-Free Massive MIMO with MEC: A Trade-Off Between Latency and Energy Consumption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: This paper investigates the trade-off between latency and energy consumption in a non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-aided cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output system that incorporates mobile edge computing (MEC). We focus on a scenario where multiple access points, each equipped with a single antenna and supported by an MEC server, collaboratively serve user equipment pairs using a power-domain NOMA strategy. The primary objective is to optimize overall system latency under power allocation constraints while minimizing energy consumption penalty. To tackle this non-convex optimization problem, we propose a two-step solution approach. The first step involves identifying optimal NOMA pairs, and the second step employs the successive convex approximation method to jointly optimize power allocation and offloading ratios. Numerical simulations are performed to validate the effectiveness of the proposed solution and to elucidate the trade-off between system latency and energy consumption.

articleTitle: A Study on a Web-Based LCA System Framework for an Environmental Impact Assessment of Consumer Electronics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics-Asia (ICCE-Asia)
abstract: Climate change threatens to undermine the past 50 years of gains in economy for consumers and productivity in the manufacture industry. The impact of manufacturing industry on the environment, which is one of the main factors affecting the environment, becomes more and more serious. LCA is used to assess environmental impacts associated with a product, process or service throughout its entire life cycle. That is to say, LCA evaluates environmental load, occurring especially in product manufacturing, in order to design and manufacture products with better environmental performance. In order to produce electronic products with such environmental performance, environmental impact assessment through LCA is necessary. In the case of electronic products, since the types and numbers of components that make up the product are numerous, the LCA work of electronic products takes up considerable time and cost. Therefore, an LCA system that provides accessibility and work convenience to users and can provide an automated workflow is required. This research is to investigate the difference of LCA software tools which used to be popular currently to reduce environmental footprint of consumer electronics. It is to suggest Web-based LCA framework that allows users to easily perform LCA tasks regardless of time and place, and consists of a web-based user interface, automated life cycle inventory generation, and simplified LCA calculations and interpretation.
